page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8y.xlarge is an arm64-based virtual server belonging to the ecs.r8y server family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Alibaba YiTian710 processor from the Yitian CPU family, operating at a clock speed of 2.75 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several computational and memory tasks. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU benchmarks register average scores of 1819.58 and 7234.41, respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show an average read-only speed of 409.68 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 59.55 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks, though large block write bandwidth is relatively weak at 24.45 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is limited, as evidenced by a poor PassMark CPU encryption score of 654.15, which correlates with the lack of advanced vector or matrix extensions, though hardware AES encryption is supported.

The instance exhibits a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require intensive floating-point or vector mathematics. However, database operations and web serving show weaker performance, with Redis SET operations reaching 6.4 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 6.29 GB/sec. This server is best suited for memory-optimized workloads such as caching layers, lightweight database operations, and general-purpose arm64 applications that benefit from dedicated CPU allocation and a larger memory footprint.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8y.xlarge is an arm64 virtual server powered by a 2.75 GHz Alibaba YiTian710 processor with 4 dedicated physical cores and 32.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance features a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core, though it lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show average CPU capabilities with a stress-ng multi-core score of 7234.41 and an average cached memory read bandwidth of 409.68 GB/sec. However, write bandwidth and cryptographic performance are relatively weak, with a PassMark encryption score of 654.15. With a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps, this memory-optimized instance is well-suited for memory-intensive arm64 workloads, caching systems, and moderate database operations.
